Question Choices: A library wants to fill 38 shelves with 5 books on each. It already has 12 books to put on these shelves. Estimate how many more books it needs to buy. Round only the shelf count to the nearest ten.
Hints: Use 40 shelves, keep 5 books per shelf and subtract the 12 books already available.
Solution: Round 38 shelves to 40; keep 5 books per shelf and 12 books already available. Estimate 40 x 5-12 = 200-12 = 188 books to buy.

Question Choices: A shop has 42 crates with 5 apples in each crate, plus 20 other apples. Estimate how many apples it has in total. Round only the crate count to the nearest ten.
Hints: Use 40 crates, multiply by 5 apples per crate, and add the 20 other apples.
Solution: Round 42 crates to 40; keep 5 apples per crate and 20 other apples. Estimate 40 x 5+20 = 200+20 = 220 apples in total.
